correctness.rationale: The orbit relation is Borel as a countable union of Borel equalizer sets, and every class is countable because it is a countable union of finite fibers. Shinko--Weilacher--Yu give hyperfiniteness under exactly the bounded-to-one countable commutative-monoid hypotheses. The classical hyperfinite equivalence-relation theorem supplies a Borel \(\mathbb Z\)-action with the same relation, whose generator is one Borel automorphism, and supplies the reduction to \(E_0\). For a nonsmooth relation, Glimm--Effros supplies the reverse reduction \(E_0\le_B E\), giving bireducibility.

evidence: The combination covers every action in the claimed class and both final conclusions.

originality.rationale: Originality fails under the required implication standard. The recent monoid theorem proves exactly that the orbit relation is hyperfinite. Classical descriptive set theory identifies countable hyperfinite Borel equivalence relations with orbit relations of a single Borel automorphism and classifies every nonsmooth hyperfinite relation at the \(E_0\) Borel degree. Therefore both advertised conclusions are immediate corollaries of the cited theorems even if the monoid paper does not restate the combined sentence.

final_claim: For every bounded-to-one Borel action of a countable commutative monoid, the induced orbit equivalence relation is generated by one Borel automorphism and is either smooth or Borel bireducible with \(E_0\).
limitations: Scientifically correct but rejected because both conclusions are immediate consequences of the cited hyperfiniteness theorem plus classical classification results.
